text:
harper: hey all, first week here! ran `rwd-kube login --env dev` and it returned a context `redwood-dev-gke-01-harper`. i switched to it but `kubectl get svc -n infra-platform-dev` is showing services from a completely different project (looks like staging). did i somehow hit the wrong cluster? :thinking:
sanjay: welcome harper! possible. can you `kubectl config view --minify --context=redwood-dev-gke-01-harper` and paste the cluster.server URL? also `kubectl config get-clusters` to see duplicates.
harper: `kubectl config view --minify --context=redwood-dev-gke-01-harper` shows `server: https://10.8.90.12` and `kubectl config get-clusters` lists `gke-redwood-01` twice (one at 10.8.90.12 and one at https://34.122.11.4). weirdly both named `gke-redwood-01`.
sanjay: ah — cluster name collision in your merged kubeconfig. earlier config fragments used a plain name `gke-redwood-01` and the new `rwd-kube` entry used the same cluster name, so kubectl is resolving the cluster reference to the first matching cluster in the merged file which can be out of date. run `kubectl config view --raw` and check the `clusters:` block ordering.
harper: yep the first cluster entry points to production IP. oof. how do i fix without blowing away my config?
devon: two safe options: 1) rename the duplicate cluster entry in your `~/.kube/config` to a unique name (e.g., `gke-redwood-01-dev`) and update the `context.cluster` fields that reference it; or 2) let `rwd-kube` write to a separate file and set KUBECONFIG to prefer the new file first: `export KUBECONFIG=$HOME/.kube/redwood:$HOME/.kube/config` then `kubectl config view --merge` should prioritize the redwood entry. I usually recommend option 2 for new hires to avoid editing old files.
harper: i had a symlink `~/.kube/config -> ~/.dotfiles/kube/config` from my old machine setup which contained the prod cluster entry first. i didn't realize it.
sanjay: that explains it. if you prefer editing, `kubectl config rename-cluster gke-redwood-01 gke-redwood-01-prod` will rename the cluster in place. then re-run `rwd-kube login --merge` and confirm contexts point to the dev cluster endpoint.
harper: tried `kubectl config rename-cluster` but then my old local contexts broke until i re-merged. switched to option 2: moved the redwood kubefile to `~/.kube/redwood` and `export KUBECONFIG=$HOME/.kube/redwood:$HOME/.kube/config` in my shell rc. `kubectl config get-contexts` now shows redwood contexts first and `kubectl cluster-info` points to the dev API.
devon: nice. two extra notes: 1) avoid editing the `clusters` ordering manually if you're not comfortable; use `kubectl config` commands so context references stay consistent. 2) we updated onboarding doc to suggest `rwd-kube login --output-file $HOME/.kube/redwood` for new machines.
kube-safety-bot: safety reminder: if you ever see a cluster server you don't recognize (private IP or unexpected public IP), pause before running destructive commands. Confirm with the platform team.
harper: thanks everyone — that was scary for a sec. changed my shell rc and verified `kubectl get pods -n infra-platform-dev` shows the expected dev pods. added a note to my onboarding checklist about symlinks and KUBECONFIG ordering. really appreciate the quick help! :tada:
